title: A κ ceiling of 2.5592e-3 for every word on #144's paired-cube design (no new κ)
body:
Adds `research/design-ceiling/` and one workflow. **No new κ, and no existing file changes.**

## Result

No word on #144's paired-cube design can certify more than

    κ < 2.5592 × 10⁻³        (complex saving a < 2.5657 × 10⁻³),

whatever its circuit, root groups, gauges, reuse pairs, terminal sinks, frames and `p`. For comparison, the selected construction on main certifies κ = 6.618855 × 10⁻⁴, so the ceiling is about 3.87 times that.

## Scope

The design is the paired-cube ports, the identity `K + H + B = I`, the coordinate-star decoder, the `K` step on the source registers and the three-stage shared cores. A word must obey the eight rules of PROOF.md §3.4. They describe #144's word format, as checked by `scripts/paired_cube/verify.py`, the frame-and-reuse layer of #155–#168 and the terminal-sink gate of #168.

**Not covered:**

- **Source-assisted words** (#184, #191, #193, #194). They use the original source registers as controls and reuse registers after exact cancellation, which breaks rules R1, R2 and R7.
- A different decoder, port family or stage structure.
- The bit supplier. The bound is on the complex saving, and κ is also below the bit saving.

## Argument

Write `D = 2v − 3ℓ` for the deficit and `C = Σ n_r·r·ln(m/r)` for the cost of the ledger's children. Every certified saving satisfies `a < D/C` (from `e^x ≥ 1 + x`), and both assemblies on main force `κ < a/(1+a)`. So it is enough to show that every word pays at least `C(p)`.

The floor comes from one structural fact: along any path of a source value from its injection to a target, frames never decrease. Three lemmas follow, for every `p ≥ 7`.

- **Every source enters at its own line.** Its role's register starts at dimension 1 and must climb to the full space.
- **Every source needs two registers that leave its line and stop again before the full space.** One subspace larger than the line misses at least `4(p−3)` of the source's targets.
- **Every target needs two registers at its own hyperplane, or an extra stop of its own register.**

A charging argument adds these to the fixed cost of the data registers. Each ingredient lowers the ceiling:

| Floor | Ceiling on `a` |
|---|---:|
| data registers and star copies only | 6.3627e-3 |
| + one register per source | 4.2121e-3 |
| + a second register per source | 2.9420e-3 |
| + registers at each target's hyperplane | 2.7868e-3 |
| + source roles enter from frame 0 | 2.7653e-3 |
| **+ the `K` itinerary of the source registers** | **2.5657e-3** |

The maximum over `p` is at `p = 13`. Every `p` from 7 to 99 is evaluated exactly, and a tail bound covers `p ≥ 100`.

[PROOF.md](https://github.com/DaysSky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/design-ceiling/research/design-ceiling/PROOF.md) is self-contained: the ledger, the rules, each lemma with its proof, the charging argument and the numbers.

## Verify

    python3 research/design-ceiling/ceiling.py --check     # the ceiling, exact; under a second
    python3 research/design-ceiling/ceiling.py --brute     # counting lemmas at small p; a few seconds
    python3 research/design-ceiling/model_check.py         # the lemmas on #144's word; about 15 seconds

All three use the standard library only and refuse `-O`.

- **`ceiling.py`** evaluates `D/C(p)` in exact rational arithmetic, with every logarithm enclosed between two rationals, and asserts the side conditions of the charging argument at every `p`.
- **`ceiling.py --brute`** enumerates the counting lemmas: over every vector at `p = 7, 8`, and over one vector from each symmetry orbit for `7 ≤ p ≤ 16`. This is a sanity check; the proofs cover every `p ≥ 7`.
- **`model_check.py`** rebuilds the proof's abstraction for the certified #144 word (`p = 12`) with the repository's own producer. It checks that the abstraction lists exactly the certified children, and that every lemma's conclusion holds on that word.

Run before opening:

- All three pass on Python 3.14 and 3.12 (macOS), and again from a clean export of the commit.
- `model_check.py --tree` also passes on a checkout of #168 (`p = 11`, with frame layer, 2,310 reuse pairs and 47 sinks).

Not run: `make verify`, and anything on Linux. The new workflow runs the three commands on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Limits

- **The proofs are by hand.** Nothing is machine-checked beyond the scripts' exact arithmetic and self-tests, and no one else has reviewed them.
- **The rules are a model of the format.** They are stated in PROOF.md §3.4 so they can be checked against the code. The model check confirms the lemmas' conclusions on two certified words; it does not prove that every acceptable word obeys the rules.
- **The ceiling is far from tight.** On #144's and #168's words the floor is 19% and 26% of the certified cost. The proof charges two registers per source; the certified words use about eight auxiliary registers per port.
- **It was not run on main's selected word** (#186), which is stored in its own archive format.

## Related

- #183 (romainhedouin) gives the assembly's acceptance ceiling in closed form. This PR bounds the supplier saving that enters it.
- #192 bounds one fixed word (#168's) over all frame layouts, at 7.010e-4. This PR bounds every word, far less tightly.
